chapter: Ragtime music and Scott Joplin books
title: Buying 25-cent band books on Charters Street
summary: Tom describes the Charters Street music stall selling sets of four books for violin, cornet and trombone.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, you told Russell about going to the music stall on Charter Street? Oh, on Charter Street, yeah. And you'd buy those 25-cent music books?
Yeah, books. Yeah, books. Yeah. It'd have sets. 25 sets of books.
Would that have the lead, or would it have the whole orchestration for the band?
It'd have a different band, 25-4 books. And you'd have everything, waltzes, charters, everything. 25 sets we used to play for. Right there, Charter and Toulouse, right on the side there.
Yeah, but would they have a part for the clarinet, a part for the violin, a part for the trumpet, or just this?

Well, they had four books there. I used to get it for the cornet and the violin. Yeah. Yeah. Oh, I see. Now they must have had it for the tram one too. But I believe I bought, I used to buy them myself, you know. Yeah. Yeah. I get four books, that cost me a dollar. I think it's for violin, cornet, and the tram one. Mm-hmm. And they had four books in the house. Mm-hmm. And we used to get all the pieces over there. We used to get it from the carpet, we used to get it from there too. Mm-hmm. But for a war line, then we started buying for a war line. But they had them using it right there on Charter Street. Mm-hmm.
